title: Eclipse Player Smart Playlist Rule
description: The stored form of a smart playlist (`playlists.rule_json`). Specification: eclipse-player.md §9.6 (REQ-PLS-010 … REQ-PLS-015). This JSON tree and the text grammar at grammars/smart-playlist.ebnf are two surfaces over one model: REQ-PLS-015 requires the visual builder and the text editor to stay in sync bidirectionally, which is only possible if one of them is canonical — this file is. Compilation target: PARAMETERISED SQL. Every literal below becomes a bound parameter; string interpolation into SQL is forbidden by REQ-PLS-010 and REQ-SEC-009 and is enforced mechanically by tools/check-sql-safety.py, so this schema needs no opinion about quoting.

limit.description: Bounded: a smart playlist is a view a user scrolls, and an unbounded rule over a large library is a UI freeze waiting to happen (REQ-PLS-014 forbids blocking the UI thread).

autoRefresh.description: REQ-PLS-014: when set, the rule is also re-evaluated at app launch, matching AIMP 4.30's behaviour.

expression.description: Either a group (AND/OR over sub-expressions, optionally negated) or a single comparison. Nesting is permitted to any depth the validator's budget allows; the grammar's parenthesised sub-expressions map onto nested groups.

not.description: The grammar's `NOT ( expression )`. Kept as a flag on the group rather than as a separate node type so the visual builder has one checkbox per row instead of an invisible wrapper.

value.description: Used by every operator except between / in / isNull / isNotNull.

caseSensitive.description: Applies to the string operators only. Default insensitive, and comparison uses the §9.2.3 normalised form, so `bjork` finds `Björk`.

allOf.description: Operand shape follows the operator: this is what makes an ill-formed rule a validation failure rather than a silently-empty playlist.

field.description: A builtin field from REQ-PLS-011, or a user-defined tag as `custom:<identifier>`. The same 37 builtin names are available to Eclipse Format Strings (REQ-EFS-007), so a user learns one vocabulary, not two.

operator.description: The REQ-PLS-011 operator set, spelled as identifiers because JSON keys are not SQL. `matches` is GLOB, never a regular expression (REQ-PLS-013): regex is a catastrophic-backtracking denial-of-service surface inside a rule a user can ship inside a playlist file or a skin.

operand.description: A literal. Which spelling is legal for a given field is decided by that field's type, not by this schema — the compiler knows `lastplayed` is a date and `duration` a length, so `'2020-01-01'` and `-30d` and `10m` are all just strings here and all become bound parameters. Ill-typed operands are rejected by the rule compiler with a message naming the field.

anyOf.description: The grammar's `ORDER BY random`. Combined with LIMIT it is how a shuffle-of-a-subset playlist is expressed.
